nodes.label: cached
nodes.rationale: Snapshot-aware cache key contract: any object derived from DATA/snapshots/<date>/ba_<year>.geojson MUST encode the snapshot identifier (basename(snapshot_dir)) in its key, because a same-named snapshot can be re-fetched with revised EFFIS perimeters (rapid mapping corrected over time), so a key omitting the snapshot would silently serve a stale .rds.

nodes.label: dominant_flag_color
nodes.rationale: Uses a fixed LOCAL seed (set.seed(1)) for reproducible k-means; the global RNG state is saved on entry and restored on.exit so calling this helper never perturbs the caller's random stream.

nodes.label: load_europe_polygons
nodes.rationale: Natural Earth sets iso_a2 = '-99' for France, Norway, Kosovo (a known dataset quirk) even though iso_a2_eh carries the correct code; the eu_keep filter is on iso_a2_eh, and iso_a2 is repaired from iso_a2_eh so downstream country codes read 'FR'/'NO'/'XK' instead of '-99'.

nodes.label: iso_week_start
nodes.rationale: Deliberately NOT as.Date(sprintf('%d-W%02d-1',...), format='%Y-%W-%u'): strptime's %V is not reliably supported for PARSING on this platform and silently returned Sys.Date() regardless of the requested week. ISO 8601 guarantees 4 January falls in week 1, so walking back to that week's Monday is a portable, dependency-free anchor.

nodes.label: get_tagged_window
nodes.rationale: Cache key = year + exact date window + snapshot (basename(snapshot_dir)) so distinct windows never collide AND a re-fetched snapshot for the same dates never serves a stale .rds. The snapshot identifier is threaded into the key for ALL years, not just the current one, because every ba_<year>.geojson can carry revised perimeters on each snapshot.

nodes.label: build_envelope
nodes.rationale: Snapshot-aware cache key so a new weekly snapshot never serves a stale envelope. The optional country arg appends a ctry_tag to the key; NULL keeps the Europe-wide behaviour AND the exact same cache key as before (backward compatible). Guards pct_vs_median against a zero/near-zero historical median-to-date (too early in season) by returning NA with a warning instead of Inf/NaN.

nodes.label: clean_polygons
nodes.rationale: Keeps every geometry stage strictly POLYGON/MULTIPOLYGON so GEOS does not fall back to slow per-element handling in downstream st_intersection/st_difference. Order matters: empties are dropped BEFORE st_collection_extract() because GEOS empties typed as GEOMETRYCOLLECTION EMPTY can make st_collection_extract silently drop ALL geometries (observed a year's ~657k ha footprint collapsing to 0 ha).

nodes.label: get_historical_footprint
nodes.rationale: Simplifies each year BEFORE unioning to keep the union tractable; st_filter() pre-screens candidates via spatial index so years with many non-European fires (Russia, North Africa) don't pay for exact intersection geometry on features that don't overlap Europe. Cache key is snapshot-aware.

nodes.label: clip_europe_year
nodes.rationale: Deliberately NOT get_tagged_full_year()/tag_countries(): tag_countries benchmarked at 3,767 s for one historical year (pairwise overlap join against ~40 country polygons), so an 11-year loop would take 10+ hours. This lighter union-only clip benchmarked at 17.6-61.3 s per year. Drops empty/degenerate geometries before area/centroid, else st_centroid returns fewer rows and desynchronises downstream vectors.

nodes.label: summarise_weekly
nodes.rationale: Order matters inside dplyr::summarise(): mean_lat (needs per-row area_ha as weights) must be computed BEFORE area_ha is overwritten by its own sum(), or area_ha collapses to a length-1 scalar and weighted.mean() throws a length mismatch (caught in smoke-testing). ISO week 53 is folded into 52 to keep every year on the same 1-52 grid.

nodes.label: build_gallery_scars
nodes.rationale: Recentres each fire's geometry on its own centroid and drops CRS so every panel renders at identical metres-per-pixel in facet_wrap. Emits a slim geometry-free meta table (rank/commune/date) BEFORE select() drops columns, so build_paris_comparison() can reuse the same top-n selection instead of recomputing. Uses month.abb[] rather than format(...,'%b') to avoid the OS locale printing non-English month abbreviations.

nodes.label: build_paris_comparison
nodes.rationale: Reuses gallery$panels (already fire_geom - fire_centroid in metres, EPSG:3035-scaled) so displacing onto Paris is just '+ paris_centroid', no geometry recompute. Reads the one-time-downloaded assets/paris_commune.geojson (INSEE 75056); if missing (fresh checkout), falls back to the same equal-area circle rather than blocking the render.

nodes.label: theme_burns
nodes.rationale: theme.R sources R/tokens.R (guarded: no-op if burns_tokens already loaded) so the ggplot theme, land-cover palette pal_lc, and brand colours all share the single YAML source theme/burns-tokens.yml.

nodes.label: burns_tokens
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth: reads theme/burns-tokens.yml (the ONE place hex values are defined) and exposes them to R so ggplot figures and the HTML/SCSS chrome cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: build_page_url
nodes.rationale: Uncapped GetFeature requests hang the server forever; every paged request must carry maxFeatures. sortby=id makes page order deterministic (MapServer's default order is not guaranteed stable) so merged pages can be safely deduped by id.

nodes.label: curl_fetch
nodes.rationale: The EFFIS server is flaky (intermittent HTTP/2 stream drops and 502/500s), so it forces HTTP/1.1 and shells out to the curl binary (not the R curl package) to enforce --http1.1/--retry exactly as tested. The URL's literal '&' separators MUST be shQuote()d or system2's shell splits the command (symptom: curl requests the bare endpoint and gets a 502 page).

nodes.label: download_year
nodes.rationale: Gets the expected feature count via resultType=hits, then pages through maxFeatures windows (sorted by id), merges pages, and dedupes by the id property as a safety net. If hits is unavailable it pages blind and stops at the first short/empty page. For current_year a zero-feature result writes an empty valid FeatureCollection (season may have barely started); any other year with zero features is a hard error.

nodes.label: latest_snapshot
nodes.rationale: Returns the newest dated snapshot directory; directory names sort correctly as strings because they follow ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD), so site pages always read the freshest fetch without hardcoding a date.

nodes.label: kv
nodes.rationale: Regenerates theme/_burns-tokens.scss from theme/burns-tokens.yml so the SCSS chrome and the R figures share ONE source of colour (registered as a Quarto pre-render step). Emits @font-face only for woff2 files that actually exist, because dart-sass aborts on a missing url() at compile time; missing fonts fall back to the system stack, keeping a fresh clone offline-safe.

nodes.label: Quarto Website Configuration
nodes.rationale: execute-dir project so all qmd chunks run from repo root and can source('R/...') and read DATA/ with root-relative paths; freeze:auto avoids recompute; pre-render regenerates the SCSS colour mirror so R figures and HTML chrome always agree with no network.

nodes.label: minty/darkly BURNS Identity Theme
nodes.rationale: burns.scss / burns-dark.scss layer the BURNS identity (surcouche) on top of the minty (light) and darkly (dark) bootswatch bases; both import the shared token mirror theme/_burns-tokens.scss so palette stays single-source.

nodes.label: CartoDB Positron Interactive Basemap
nodes.rationale: Leaflet interactive maps use addProviderTiles('CartoDB.Positron'), a neutral light basemap that keeps the fire perimeters and Paris boundary legible without competing with the tiles.

nodes.label: EFFIS Rapid Perimeters (data source)
nodes.rationale: All fire outlines come from EFFIS (Copernicus Emergency Management Service), satellite-mapped burn-scar polygons; rapid estimates that undercount small fires, are revised over time, and differ from official national statistics, so figures are exploratory not authoritative.

nodes.label: MODIS to Sentinel-2 Detection Transition
nodes.rationale: EFFIS mapping shifted from MODIS-based (~30 ha floor) to Sentinel-2-based detection, roughly doubling fire COUNTS from 2023 to 2024 as smaller fires became detectable; cross-year comparisons therefore use burned AREA (dominated by large fires, insensitive to detection threshold), not counts.

nodes.label: Country Attribution by Maximum Overlap
nodes.rationale: Each fire is assigned to the country it overlaps most (mainland-Europe crop, overseas territories excluded); EFFIS's own COUNTRY attribute is kept only as a cross-check because border-area fires can be misallocated.

nodes.label: Weekly Snapshot Pinning
nodes.rationale: Rapid mapping is revised each weekly refresh, so every page pins the exact snapshot date in its captions; a later re-render is not expected to reproduce earlier figures exactly, by design. All cache keys are snapshot-aware to close the stale-weekly-data trap.

nodes.label: Local Render-and-Publish (not CI)
nodes.rationale: The site refreshes locally via scripts/update_site.sh, not GitHub Actions, because EFFIS's WFS server is too flaky for unattended CI (hangs, intermittent 502/500), per-year GeoJSON snapshots are too heavy for the repo (few MB to >100 MB, DATA/snapshots git-ignored), and rnaturalearthhires ships only from r-universe not CRAN.

nodes.label: Cumulative Burned-Area Envelope
nodes.rationale: 2026 cumulative burned area since 1 June against the 2017-2025 min-max band and median; a 'race against the past' using the identical 1 Jun to 30 Sep window every year so seasons compare like for like.

nodes.label: Weekly Calendar Heatmap
nodes.rationale: Weekly Europe-clipped burned area by ISO week, 2016-2026; includes 2016 (unlike the comparison band) because a full-decade grid is the point, with 2016 captioned as lower-confidence; sqrt fill scale so true-zero weeks display and July-August peaks stay compressed enough to keep smaller months visible.

nodes.label: Hero + Period-Facet Perimeter Maps
nodes.rationale: All 2026 Europe-clipped perimeters (1 Jan to as-of), plus a January-May vs summer-window facet, exposing the unusually busy late-winter/spring surge alongside the familiar summer block.

nodes.label: Interactive Leaflet Fire Explorer
nodes.rationale: Pan/zoom map of every 2026 fire, shapes simplified to ~100 m tolerance for page speed; GEOMETRYCOLLECTION rows split to polygon parts and line slivers dropped because leaflet only draws polygonal geometry; sliver-drop share computed as a real inline value.

nodes.label: Fire-Size Distribution
nodes.rationale: Two panels on a shared log size axis: count of fires per size band (weight on the left, most fires under 30 ha) vs hectares burned (weight on the right, a few giants hold nearly all area); motivates measuring area over counts.

nodes.label: Gallery of Scars (top-10 fires)
nodes.rationale: The ten largest 2026 fires each drawn at the same metric scale with a Paris-area reference circle (~105 km2 / 10,500 ha), coloured by dominant land cover, so true relative size is directly comparable.

nodes.label: Paris Comparator (drop each fire onto Paris)
nodes.rationale: Each top-10 fire's true outline is translated onto the real Paris municipal boundary (INSEE 75056, from france-geojson/Etalab), one fire at a time via radio-style layer control (hideGroup all but the first), so size is compared against the actual city rather than a circle. Reuses gallery geometry rather than re-simplifying.
nodes.norm_label: paris comparator (drop each fire onto paris)

nodes.label: Top-10 Country Rankings
nodes.rationale: Top-10 countries by Europe-clipped burned area (raw hectares, left) and as a share of national land area (right, a fairer normalization); flag PNGs drawn with base annotation_raster; factor levels set after the flag join so bar order and flag y-positions are not scrambled.

nodes.label: Re-burn Map (old-scar overlap)
nodes.rationale: 2026 perimeters split into first-time burns vs re-burns of ground already inside a merged 2017-2025 historical footprint; overlap on ~100 m-simplified EPSG:3035 geometry. Describes overlap, not land-condition severity.

nodes.label: Land-Cover Composition
nodes.rationale: Land-cover shares of burned area in the 1 June to as-of window: 2026 vs the pooled area-weighted 2017-2025 average for the identical window; each perimeter's land-cover percentages weighted by its Europe-clipped area. Reads as what burned, not what burns easily.

nodes.label: Natura 2000 Protected-Area Analysis
nodes.rationale: Season-by-season area-weighted share of burned area inside a Natura 2000 site (EFFIS's PERCNA2K field), same 1 June cutoff every year for fairness, plus a map colouring 2026 perimeters by their protected-area share.

nodes.label: France and Spain Country Envelopes
nodes.rationale: The cumulative-envelope 'race against the past' repeated per country for France and Spain (the two carrying most of 2026), each against its own 2017-2025 range rather than Europe's.

nodes.label: Season-at-a-glance Headline Numbers
nodes.rationale: Three headline figures (burned area since 1 June, fire count, percent vs recent-season median) plus the shared envelope chart; reads the SAME cached envelope object as posts/2026.qmd via an identical build_envelope cache key so nothing heavy is recomputed.
